chapters.title: The language classroom
chapters.subtitle: You arrive at a language school and meet the other learners.

chapters.title: Around the school
chapters.subtitle: Find your way, describe what you see and talk about where you live.

chapters.title: At lunch and in town
chapters.subtitle: Talk to classmates and ask for help or something to drink.

chapters.title: Plans for today
chapters.subtitle: Say what you can do, what you want to do and what you are doing today.

chapters.title: What happened yesterday?
chapters.subtitle: Tell a classmate about yesterday and finish with a short review.

lessons.title: Learn a noun with its article
lessons.goal: Find the card for “the table” and choose its dictionary form.
explanation: Learn each noun together with its article: «der», «die» or «das». Examples: «der Stuhl», «die Lampe», «das Buch».
The dictionary form uses the nominative. Open a card and place a chip on Nominativ before playing it.

lessons.title: Choose a form of sein
lessons.goal: Choose the “I” form of “to be”.
explanation: A verb changes with the person. You say «ich bin» (I am), «du bist» (you are) and «sie ist» (she is).
Open the «sein» card and put a chip on the line with the right person. This exercise needs only one card.

lessons.title: Choose the person you mean
lessons.goal: Point to one classmate informally. Play “you” as the subject.
explanation: Pick «du» for one person you know or address informally. Use «ihr» for several people and «Sie» in formal situations.
The subject is in the nominative. Select it in the pronoun card.

lessons.title: Build your first sentence
lessons.goal: You arrive at the classroom. Say “I’m coming”.
explanation: A simple statement can start with the subject, followed by the conjugated verb. The subject chip is Nominativ.
For «ich», choose the «ich» form on the verb card. Compare «Ich lerne.» (I’m learning).

lessons.title: Ask someone’s name
lessons.goal: You meet a classmate. Ask “What’s your name?”
explanation: A question word starts the question. Put the conjugated verb right after it and the subject after the verb.
The question about someone’s name uses «wie» and «heißen». Another example: «Wo wohnst du?»

lessons.title: Recognise the direct object
lessons.goal: In your classroom picture, say “The man is eating the apple”.
explanation: Use nominative for the subject and accusative for the direct object of «essen». Ask who is eating and what he is eating.
In masculine singular, the definite article changes from «der» to «den». Compare «der Tisch» and «den Tisch».

lessons.title: Say where you are coming from
lessons.goal: Tell a classmate “I’m coming from the school”.
explanation: The preposition «aus» expresses origin and takes the dative. The article «die» changes to «der» in feminine singular.
Compare «aus dem Haus» (from the house).

lessons.title: Say where someone is going
lessons.goal: Describe the morning scene. Say “The child is going into the school”.
explanation: With «in», use the accusative when the phrase gives the destination and answers «Wohin?» (where to?).
Compare «in das Haus» for a destination with «in dem Haus» for a location.
lessons.targetSentence: Das Kind geht in die Schule.

lessons.title: Say where you are
lessons.goal: Someone calls you. Say “I’m at the school”.
explanation: A location answers «Wo?» (where?). With «in», that calls for the dative. Compare «Das Buch ist auf dem Tisch.»
Keep «in» and its noun next to each other on the sentence strip.

lessons.title: Describe what you see
lessons.goal: You are looking at classroom furniture. Say “The table is high”.
explanation: After «sein», an adjective needs no ending for gender or number. Compare «Das Buch ist neu.» and «Die Bücher sind neu.» For a description without a comparison, place the chip on «Grundform».

lessons.title: Talk about more than one
lessons.goal: The classroom has new books. Say “The books are new”.
explanation: The nominative plural article is «die». Learn each noun with its plural: «das Kind» becomes «die Kinder».
A plural subject takes the «sie / Sie» line on the verb card. Your hand contains a ready-made plural card. Choose «Grundform» on the adjective.

lessons.title: Ask a polite yes/no question
lessons.goal: Ask a visitor politely “Are you drinking the water?”
explanation: Start a yes/no question with the conjugated verb. Place the subject immediately after it.
Formal «Sie» always begins with a capital letter. Its verb form uses the same line as plural «sie».

lessons.title: Replace a noun with a pronoun
lessons.goal: You’ve already mentioned the apple. Say “I’m eating it”.
explanation: Use a pronoun when the listener knows which thing you mean. «Der Apfel» is masculine, so choose the row for «er».
As the direct object of «essen», the masculine pronoun changes from «er» to «ihn».

lessons.title: Ask someone to help you
lessons.goal: Ask a classmate “Are you helping me?” Use informal “you”.
explanation: Start the yes/no question with the verb. After «helfen», the person receiving help is in the dative.
Compare «ich» (I), «mich» (me, accusative) and «mir» (me, dative).

lessons.title: Say who is with you
lessons.goal: Tell a classmate “I’m coming with you”. Use informal “you”.
explanation: «Mit» takes the dative. On the «du» card, compare «du», «dich» and «dir».

lessons.title: Say what you want to do
lessons.goal: You’re making plans with a classmate. Say “I want to play”.
explanation: Conjugate «wollen» to show who wants something, then put the other verb at the end in its dictionary form.
Choose the Infinitiv chip on the final verb card. Compare «Du kannst kommen.»

lessons.title: Start with a time word
lessons.goal: Say “Today we are learning”. Put “today” first.
explanation: A time word such as «heute» can come first. The conjugated verb stays in position two, and the subject moves after it.
Compare «Wir lernen heute.» and «Heute lernen wir.»

lessons.title: Split a separable verb
lessons.goal: Say “I’m shopping today”. Start with “today”.
explanation: In a present-tense statement, «einkaufen» splits. The conjugated part stays in position two and «ein» goes at the end.
Play one card for «einkaufen» and a second card for the prefix. Compare «Wir kaufen ein.»

lessons.title: Say what you aren’t doing
lessons.goal: Say “I’m not coming today”. Start with “today”.
explanation: Use «nicht» to negate an action. In a short sentence like «Ich komme nicht.», it goes at the end.
With a modal verb, «nicht» comes before the final infinitive in «Ich kann nicht kommen.»

lessons.title: Talk about yesterday with haben
lessons.goal: Say “I studied yesterday”. Start with “yesterday”.
explanation: To talk about the past in conversation, use the Perfekt. Conjugate «haben» and put the past participle at the end.
Choose Partizip II on the final card. Compare «Wir haben gespielt.»

lessons.title: Talk about an arrival
lessons.goal: Say “We arrived yesterday”. Start with “yesterday”.
explanation: The «kommen» card shows which helper verb to use for the Perfekt. Choose the «wir» form of that helper.
Compare «Ich bin gegangen.» (I left) and «Ich habe gelernt.» (I studied).

lessons.title: Compare the two participles
lessons.goal: Find the present participle of “to play”.
explanation: Partizip I is the present participle: «spielend» (playing). Partizip II is the past participle: «gespielt» (played).
For the Perfekt, look for Partizip II. Here, choose Partizip I as a card-reading exercise.

lessons.title: Finish with a question
lessons.goal: Ask a classmate “Can you come with me today?” Start with the verb.
explanation: Begin with the yes/no question form. Put the subject right after the finite verb, then say when and with whom.
Recall which case follows «mit» and which form closes a sentence with a modal verb.
lessons.targetSentence: Kannst du heute mit mir kommen?
